metadata.title: Volcanic Soils Emergency Knowledge Base - Degraded Andosol / High-Acid Pumice Basin
metadata.author: Agricultural Engineering Practice Unit - Volcanic Soils (Andosols)
metadata.scope: Diagnostics and remediation (precision liming, biochar, phosphorus liberation, slope erosion control), sub-25-day emergency protein, high-yield starch root crop strategy, ranked top-5 crops, and a beginner cultivation roadmap for a degraded high-acid volcanic ash / pumice basin.

units.ph: pH units (1:2.5 soil:water suspension; buffer pH measured in parallel for lime requirement)
units.amendment_rate: t/ha or kg/ha as stated; liming expressed as t/ha CaCO3 equivalent (CaCO3e)
units.time: days relative to Day 0 (= main starch crop planting day); negative values are pre-plant

metadata.parse_guide: Chain: scenario_input -> soil_parameters.ph / soil_parameters.ec_ds_m / soil_parameters.slope_and_erosion / soil_parameters.phosphorus_status range match -> diagnostic_rules sorted by ascending priority (first rule with modifier=false whose when-clause matches = base_condition; every matched rule with modifier=true appends its then-value as a modifier code) -> soil_conditions[base_condition] plus soil_conditions[each modifier] -> treatment_protocols[each matched code] combined with remediation_treatment (precision module for this scenario) -> crop_recommendations[base+modifiers joined by '+'] -> cultivation_roadmaps[where target_condition contains the matched codes]. Fields named *_ref are dotted-path pointers to other keys. All rate objects use {min,max,unit} for programmatic consumption.

safety_guards.then: HALT this protocol; salinity reclamation (leaching + drainage) must precede liming - refer to a salinity knowledge base
Do NOT compute lime from water pH alone; on high-organic, high-P-fixing ash soils water pH mis-estimates lime requirement by 30-50%
Skip corrective liming; apply maintenance lime only (0.5-1.0 t/ha CaCO3e per year)

safety_guards.if: slope > 25% OR rills are actively extending during rainfall
safety_guards.then: Install structural erosion control (vetiver contour hedgerows + jute/coir netting + mulch) BEFORE any tillage, incorporation or traffic

safety_guards.if: cassava (Manihot esculenta) product is destined for human consumption
safety_guards.then: Never eat raw: peel, chip, soak or ferment 24-48 h, then boil or sun-dry (cyanogenic glycosides); sweet/low-cyanide clones preferred in emergencies

standards_referenced: FAO - World Reference Base for Soil Resources (WRB): Andosols, volcanic ash materials
USDA - Soil Survey Manual / Soil Taxonomy (Andisols; pH class boundaries; exchanger acidity)
Kamprath - buffer pH (lime requirement) methodology for acid soils
IFDC / IPNI - Reactive Phosphate Rock direct application guidance (fineness, soil pH, placement)
IBI - International Biochar Initiative standards (H:C ratio, pH, liming value, contaminant limits)
Vetiver Network / FAO - vetiver grass technology for contour hedgerows and gully control
USDA NRCS - Field Book for Describing and Sampling Soils (erosion classes, slope classes)
ICAR / IIPR - acid soil crop and nutrient recommendation guidelines (Ca, Mg, Mo, banded P)
Mycorrhizal Applications / IBI - arbuscular mycorrhizal inoculant quality and placement guidelines
metadata.disclaimer: All rates are decision-support defaults for an assumed non-saline (ECe < 0.75 dS/m) degraded volcanic ash basin. Field application must be preceded by a current laboratory soil test (pH, buffer pH, exchangeable Al/Ca/Mg/K, Olsen or Truog P, organic C, and ideally oxalate-extractable Al+Fe for degree of P saturation). Lime and biochar rates must be finalised from buffer-pH and exchangeable-base data, never from water pH alone.

scenario_input.soil_profile: Degraded Volcanic Ash / High-Acid Pumice Basin

classification.parent_material: Weathered pumice, ash and tephra layers

measured.ec_assumed: non-saline (<0.75 dS/m) - degraded, strongly leached basin

ph.measurement: pH in 1:2.5 soil:water suspension; record buffer pH (SMP/Kehres/York) separately for lime-rate calculation

ranges.label: Very Strongly Acidic
ranges.risk: Severe Al3+/Mn2+ toxicity, base-cation leaching, extreme P fixation, Mo deficiency

ranges.label: Strongly Acidic
ranges.risk: Exchangeable Al dominates the exchange complex; Ca/Mg/K depleted; P fixed by Al and allophane - SCENARIO MATCH at pH 4.6

ranges.label: Moderately Acidic
ranges.risk: Al toxicity declining but still present; P fixation, Mn toxicity risk, reduced nitrification

ranges.label: Slightly Acidic
ranges.risk: Marginal - TARGET BAND for acid volcanic soils (5.5-6.0): Al neutralised, P availability and reactive rock phosphate dissolution both near optimum

ranges.label: Mildly Acidic
ranges.risk: Low; maintain organic matter and Mg supply

ranges.label: Neutral
ranges.note: Do NOT over-lime volcanic ash beyond 6.5: micronutrient availability falls and allophane anion sorption rises

ranges.label: Moderately Alkaline
ranges.risk: P precipitated as Ca-phosphate; micronutrient chlorosis

ec_ds_m.measurement: ECe = saturated-paste extract. Soil:water 1:5 suspensions are not interchangeable with ECe.

ranges.label: Saline
ranges.action: Trigger safety guard G-01 - leach salts before liming

ranges.label: Strongly to Very Strongly Saline
ranges.action: Trigger safety guard G-01 - reclamation required

slope_and_erosion.measurement: Combination of slope grade, vegetative ground cover and USDA erosion class

ranges.label: Moderate
ranges.action: Contour hedgerows + cover crop + residue retention

ranges.label: Severe
ranges.action: Emergency structural + organic stabilisation before any planting - SCENARIO MATCH

slope_and_erosion.note: Severity is driven as much by cover deficit as by gradient: slope >5% with cover <30% and active rills = EROSION_SEVERE regardless of absolute slope.

phosphorus_status.measurement: Olsen or Truog P (preferred for acid volcanic soils; Bray under-reports on high-sorbing media). Degree of P saturation (DPS) by ammonium oxalate = (Al_ox + Fe_ox based) for andisols.

ranges.label: P-deficient / strongly fixing
ranges.action: Band soluble starter P + reactive rock phosphate + AMF

ranges.label: P-low
ranges.action: Banded P at every planting; sidedress at 45-60 days

ranges.label: P-adequate (andisol target)
ranges.action: Maintain with band P and organic matter - SCENARIO TARGET
ranges.note: Andisols are safely held at DPS 15-25%, higher than the 10-15% used for crystalline soils, because allophane binds P without toxicity risk

ranges.label: P-high
ranges.action: Suspend P applications; test runoff risk

diagnostic_rules.evidence: pH <4.5: exchangeable Al dominant, base saturation <35%, Ca/Mg leached from ash

diagnostic_rules.description: Strongly acid, non-saline - scenario base condition
diagnostic_rules.evidence: pH 4.5-5.0: Al toxicity well advanced, Mn risk, Ca/Mg/K depletion, P fixation - liming indicated (pH 4.6 = MATCH)
Al present but declining; P fixation persists - corrective or maintenance liming by buffer pH
Salts must be leached before lime reacts correctly - safety guard G-01

diagnostic_rules.description: Non-saline but high-P-fixing short-range-order mineral present
diagnostic_rules.evidence: Allophane/imogolite and amorphous Fe/Al oxides sorb phosphate by ligand exchange; broadcast P is locked up - overlay on the acid diagnosis

diagnostic_rules.description: Active severe erosion on sloping land
diagnostic_rules.evidence: Sheet/rill erosion is removing the A horizon that holds the little available P - overlay alongside the pH diagnosis

diagnostic_rules.description: Slightly to mildly acidic, non-saline, no modifiers
diagnostic_rules.evidence: Agronomically acceptable - this is the post-remediation target state
Unexpected for this soil type - verify meter calibration and request a full exchangeable-cation and ESP test
No specific rule matched - request a full soil test before amending

ACID_LOW_BASE.name: Strongly Acidic, Low-Base-Saturation Volcanic Soil
ACID_LOW_BASE.definition: pH < 5.5, ECe < 0.75 dS/m, base saturation < 50%, exchangeable Al3+ significant above pH 5.0
ACID_LOW_BASE.typical_causes: Intense leaching of bases from pumice/ash; acid parent material; legacy ammonium fertiliser; removal of bases by cropping and burning
ACID_LOW_BASE.symptoms: Pruned, stubby roots with blackened tips (Al), poor tillering, purple/red tinting on young leaves (P deficiency induced by Al), Ca/Mg deficiency, crop responds sharply to lime
ACID_LOW_BASE.diagnostic_thresholds: Exchangeable Al > 0.5 cmol(c)/kg or Al saturation > 20%; Ca+Mg < 2.0 cmol(c)/kg; buffer pH below the lime-requirement target

P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.name: Allophane / Volcanic Phosphate Fixation
P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.definition: Short-range-order allophane, imogolite and amorphous Fe/Al oxides sorb phosphate so rapidly that broadcast P is largely unavailable
P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.typical_causes: Young/weakly weathered volcanic ash and pumice (Andosols); acidic conditions keeping Al/Fe oxide edges reactive
P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.symptoms: Soil test P low despite a history of P application; crops respond strongly to banded starter P; high anion-exchange capacity; very high P retention
P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.diagnostic_thresholds: Ammonium-oxalate Al+Fe > 1.0% (allophane > 6-8%); P retention index > 85%; DPS (oxalate) < 15-20%; Olsen/Truog P < 15 mg/kg

EROSION_SEVERE.name: Severe Slope Erosion
EROSION_SEVERE.definition: Active sheet/rill erosion on >5% slope with <30% ground cover
EROSION_SEVERE.typical_causes: Bare tilled or burnt slopes after clearing; high-intensity rainfall on low-density pumice/ash; downhill tillage and wheel traffic
EROSION_SEVERE.symptoms: Exposed subsoil, rills, sediment fans, thin or absent A horizon, litter-free surface, water running turbid after every storm

MARGINALLY_ACIDIC.name: Mildly Acidic Soil (post-remediation target state)
MARGINALLY_ACIDIC.typical_causes: Successful liming and organic matter build
MARGINALLY_ACIDIC.symptoms: Good vigour; maintain pH and Mg with maintenance lime

HEALTHY.name: Healthy / Agronomically Optimal Soil
HEALTHY.symptoms: Normal crop vigour, good tilth, biological activity

OUT_OF_SCOPE_SALINITY.name: Salinity detected - protocol halt
OUT_OF_SCOPE_SALINITY.action: Stop acid-soil remediation; leach salts and restore drainage first (safety guard G-01). Liming fails while salts remain.

UNDIAGNOSED.name: Insufficient data
UNDIAGNOSED.definition: No diagnostic rule matched, or required inputs (buffer pH, EC, Al) are missing
UNDIAGNOSED.action: Collect a full laboratory soil test (pH, buffer pH, ECe, exchangeable Al/Ca/Mg/K, Olsen P, organic C) and re-run diagnosis

ACID_LOW_BASE.objective: Raise pH to 5.5-6.0 (target 5.8), neutralise exchangeable Al, restore Ca/Mg/K and rebuild organic matter

amendments.input: Corrective agricultural lime (rate from BUFFER pH)

escalation_rate.unit: t/ha CaCO3e (pH <4.5 or exchangeable Al > 2.5 cmol/kg)

amendments.method: Split 60-70% basal incorporated 0-15 cm, 30-40% topdress at 60-90 days if buffer pH still low
Use <= 0.15 mm grind (reacts 2-3x slower than calcitic); never apply together with ammonium fertiliser

amendments.input: Gypsum (subsoil Al, or where lime cannot be worked deep)
amendments.method: Deep placement or with irrigation water - supplies Ca without raising pH
Broadcast, light incorporation; buffers pH, chelates Al, adds Ca and bases
Seed treatment or 0.1% foliar - restores legume N fixation in acid soil
Soil or 0.5% foliar x2
Banded 5 cm below seed/sett - never broadcast on acid high-Al soil

ACID_LOW_BASE.erosion_control: Mulch 5-8 t/ha; contour strips; close-cover legumes to stop base-cation leaching
ACID_LOW_BASE.do_not: Do not use ammonium nitrate/sulphate as the sole N source (further acidification); do not plough on the fall line; do not burn residues; do not over-lime beyond pH 6.5
ACID_LOW_BASE.follow_up: Re-test pH, buffer pH and exchangeable Al after 6-8 weeks (lime acts over 4-8 weeks)

P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.objective: Beat the phosphate sink: lift pH to 5.5-5.8 to reduce Al/Fe reactivity, place P where roots reach it, and use organic matter and mycorrhiza to compete for and bridge sorption sites

amendments.method: Incorporate 6-8 weeks before planting - cuts exchangeable Al and allophane P-sorption capacity
Fineness 80-90% passing 0.15 mm; banded into the moist root zone - dissolves best at pH 4.5-6.0 and feeds roots continuously for 6-12 months
STRICTLY BANDED: 5 cm below and 5 cm to the side of the sett/seed - the localised high concentration saturates sorption sites

amendments.input: Compost / FYM + biochar (competes with P for sorption)
amendments.method: Incorporate in the row; humic/fulvic fractions desorb P

rate.unit: kg/ha granular (or 20-50 g per planting hole)

amendments.method: Applied in the planting hole, ideally carried on charged biochar - extends the effective P-depletion zone 3-10x
Banded at 45-60 days
NH4 uptake lowers rhizosphere pH and liberates sorbed P

P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.erosion_control: On eroded allophane slopes the P-rich ash topsoil washes off first - mulch heavily and never leave bare fallow
P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.notes: Target DPS 15-25% for andisols. Expect only 15-40% recovery of fertiliser P - banding is what makes applied P pay. Soluble P in direct contact with the inoculant suppresses AMF colonisation; keep soluble starter P at or below ~30 kg P2O5/ha in the hole.
P_FIXATION_ALLOPHANE.follow_up: Olsen P at 45 and 90 days; re-band if Olsen P < 12 mg/kg

EROSION_SEVERE.objective: Stop soil loss immediately, then rebuild the A horizon

amendments.method: Continuous organic blanket - cuts raindrop impact 80-95%

amendments.rate: 1 line per 5-10 m vertical interval (5 m on slopes >15% or where rills are active); 2-3 slips per station at 0.3-0.5 m in-line spacing
amendments.method: Plant slips on the contour; hedges trap sediment, dissipate runoff and re-level the slope
amendments.timing: First rains / start of wet season

amendments.input: Jute / coir erosion netting and biodegradable stakes
amendments.rate: cover 100% of bare or rilled ground
amendments.method: Staple along the contour over freshly exposed soil and rill lines

amendments.input: Cover crop / living mulch (Mucuna, Crotalaria, Stylosanthes, cowpea, sweet potato)
amendments.method: Broadcast or row-interseed - reach 100% cover within 45-60 days
Applied under mulch on the contour - do NOT deep-incorporate on a slope

amendments.input: Grassed waterways, contour bunds, check dams
amendments.rate: waterway 3-5 m wide; contour bunds/tied ridges on 5-10% slopes; bench terraces >15% (FAO)
amendments.method: Permanent grass in drainage lines; small brush/stone check dams in active rills

EROSION_SEVERE.do_not: No clean tillage, no burning, no downhill ploughing, no wheel traffic on wet slopes, no bare inter-row soil after canopy closure
EROSION_SEVERE.follow_up: Photograph fixed points monthly; inspect after every storm; add 2-3 t/ha compost each season until the A horizon recovers

MARGINALLY_ACIDIC.objective: Hold pH at 5.8-6.5 and rebuild organic matter

amendments.method: Surface apply under mulch (no incorporation needed)
Broadcast
Row banded

MARGINALLY_ACIDIC.erosion_control: Residue retention; keep cover crops between cash crops

HEALTHY.objective: Sustain organic matter, cover and structure

amendments.method: Broadcast and incorporate at land prep
Split N; band P and K

HEALTHY.erosion_control: Maintain >= 70% ground cover at all times; contour farming on any slope
HEALTHY.follow_up: Soil test every 12 months; watch pH drift from acid N fertilisers

amendments.input: Leaching with good-quality water (ECw < 0.7 dS/m) + drainage
amendments.method: Ponded leaching with working outlet
Broadcast or dissolved in irrigation

OUT_OF_SCOPE_SALINITY.erosion_control: Mulch during leaching to prevent crusting and salt-laden runoff
OUT_OF_SCOPE_SALINITY.follow_up: Re-enter this knowledge base only after ECe < 0.75 dS/m

amendments.input: Full soil test (pH, buffer pH, ECe, exchangeable Al/Ca/Mg/K, Olsen P, organic C, optional oxalate Al+Fe)
amendments.rate: 1 composite sample per management unit (20-25 cores, 0-15 cm)
amendments.method: Grid or zone sampling; record slope and erosion class with each sample

UNDIAGNOSED.erosion_control: Apply emergency mulch and netting regardless of test results (safe under all diagnoses)

remediation_treatment.objective: Convert a severely acidic (pH 4.6), phosphate-fixing, actively eroding ash/pumice surface into a plantable seedbed at pH 5.5-6.0 with plant-available P and a stable soil surface, in one 60-day pre-plant window.

target_ph.rationale: Neutralises exchangeable Al and maximises P availability while keeping reactive rock phosphate dissolving and micronutrients available; do not exceed 6.5 on andisols

liming_program.rate_determination: Lime rate (t/ha CaCO3e) = f(buffer pH, exchangeable Al, CEC/texture) from the local lime-requirement table (SMP/Kehres/York). Water pH alone must not be used (guard G-02).

base_rate.condition: topsoil pH 4.6, loam/silt-loam ash, exchangeable Al 0.5-2.5 cmol/kg

high_requirement_rate.condition: pH < 4.5, exchangeable Al > 2.5 cmol/kg, or very low base saturation (< 25%)

expected_response.condition: lime fineness >= 90% passing 0.85 mm; best results at <= 0.15 mm

calcitic_lime.chemical: CaCO3 (approx 36-38% Ca; effective calcium carbonate ECC 90-100%)
calcitic_lime.use_when: exchangeable Mg >= 1.5 cmol/kg OR Mg saturation >= 15% of CEC OR soil has a known Mg history (volcanic ash recently fertilised with dolomitic lime or K-mag fertilisers)
calcitic_lime.advantage: Fast-acting, no Mg-K antagonism, safe where Mg is adequate

dolomitic_lime.use_when: exchangeable Mg < 1.0 cmol/kg OR Mg saturation < 10% of CEC OR Ca:Mg ratio > 10:1 - the DEFAULT for strongly leached pumice basins, where Mg has been washed out with the bases
dolomitic_lime.advantage: Corrects Mg deficiency in one pass - Mg is required for chlorophyll and Mg-deficiency is common on leached ash soils
dolomitic_lime.caution: Reacts 2-3x slower than calcitic - use a fine grind (<= 0.15 mm); do not exceed 1.5x the calcitic rate; excess Mg antagonises K uptake

type_decision_table.extra: Add Mg as kieserite (MgSO4) 10-20 kg Mg/ha if Mg < 0.5
Protect Mg by keeping mulch and reduced leaching

liming_program.split_application: 60-70% basal incorporated 0-15 cm at Day -60; 30-40% topdressed at Day +60 if buffer pH still indicates a deficit
liming_program.sloped_ground_rule: On >5% slopes do not mouldboard or deep-till to incorporate: spread lime under the mulch layer or work it into contour furrows/beds only - tillage on the fall line would accelerate the erosion being treated
safety_rules: Never apply lime and ammonium fertiliser together or within 14 days (volatilisation of NH3 as pH rises)
Do not apply more than 4 t/ha in a single event; split heavy requirements
Water lime into the soil after spreading, or apply before rain; never allow dry lime dust to blow off a slope
Store lime covered - weathered lime loses reactivity
liming_program.biochar_liming_credit: Subtract 0.05-0.20 t CaCO3e per tonne of high-pH (pH >= 9) wood biochar from the calculated lime rate

purpose: Permanent raise of CEC and pH buffering (ash soils have low native CEC)
Sequesters stable carbon and rebuilds degraded topsoil
Adsorbs and slowly releases bases, reducing leaching losses on slopes
Improves plant-available water in pumice (typical gain 10-25%)
Habitat and carrier for mycorrhizal fungi and rhizobia

rate.note: Higher rates (10-15 t/ha) only in beds and planting rows; on severe slopes prefer 5 t/ha incorporated plus 2-3 t/ha as a surface conditioner under mulch

biochar_program.fineness: Particles < 2 mm for rapid reaction; coarser (2-10 mm) acceptable for long-term structure
biochar_program.quality_spec: Per IBI: pH >= 8, H:C(org) <= 0.4, C >= 50%, ash-limited, no PAH or heavy-metal exceedance; wood/feedstock biochar preferred over manure-derived on food crops
biochar_program.pre_charging_mandatory: NEVER apply fresh biochar. Age 2-4 weeks: co-compost at a biochar:feedstock ratio of 1:2 (e.g. 5 t biochar + 10 t manure/compost) or soak in nutrient/compost tea until the material is wetted and microbially inoculated. Fresh biochar adsorbs soil N and P, blows as dust, and can carry phytotoxic volatiles.
biochar_program.application_method: Incorporate the charged material in the top 0-15 cm at bed preparation, or surface-apply 2-3 t/ha under the mulch on slopes where tillage is prohibited; band the highest rate in the planting row
biochar_program.p_fixation_caveat: Fresh, high-ash biochar can itself sorb phosphate; only charged/co-composted biochar with a high base-cation load has a net P benefit on allophane soil

phosphorus_liberation_program.diagnosis_required: Olsen/Truog P, plus ammonium-oxalate Al+Fe and DPS if available; target Olsen P 15-25 mg/kg and DPS 15-25% for andisols
phosphorus_liberation_program.strategy: Three-layer approach: (1) reactive rock phosphate as a slow, continuous acid-dissolved source, (2) a concentrated soluble starter band to saturate the immediate sorption sites, (3) AMF plus organic matter to extend and protect the P-depletion zone.

reactive_phosphate_rock.input: Finely ground reactive (soft) phosphate rock (30-36% P2O5)
reactive_phosphate_rock.fineness: 80-90% passing 0.15 mm; finer is more reactive

soil_ph_window.note: Acid dissolution of carbonate-apatite is fastest below pH 6.0 - the remediated pH 5.5-5.8 is ideal

reactive_phosphate_rock.placement: Banded 10-15 cm below the planting row, into moist soil

soluble_starter.input: Single superphosphate (16-18% P2O5, also supplies S and Ca) or TSP
soluble_starter.placement: STRICT band: 5 cm below and 5 cm to the side of sett/seed - never broadcast on allophane soil

mycorrhizal_inoculant.type: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF): Rhizophagus irregularis, Glomus mosseae / Funneliformis mosseae, Claroideoglomus etunicatum, Gigaspora spp.

rate.unit: kg/ha granular (20-50 g per planting hole)

mycorrhizal_inoculant.carrier: Charged biochar or peat carrier - biochar improves hyphal survival and is the preferred on-slope carrier
mycorrhizal_inoculant.placement: Directly on the sett base / root zone at planting, covered immediately
mycorrhizal_inoculant.why_critical: Degraded, burnt or heavily tilled ash soils have very low native mycorrhizal inoculum; AMF extend the effective P-depletion zone 3-10x and are the only biological route to the phosphate locked in allophane
compatibility_rules: Co-apply with rock phosphate (not with heavy soluble P) - high soluble P in the hole suppresses colonisation; keep in-hole soluble P at or below ~30 kg P2O5/ha
Do not mix with high-rate DAP or superphosphate in direct contact
Avoid broad-spectrum soil fungicides and high-rate nitrification-inhibitor residues near the inoculant
Inoculate legumes and tubers alike - AMF response is largest on P-fixing soils

organic_competitors.function: Humic and fulvic fractions compete with phosphate for allophane sorption sites and desorb already-fixed P

phosphorus_liberation_program.rhizosphere_management: Favour a mild NH4-N contribution or use a nitrification inhibitor: NH4 uptake acidifies the rhizosphere and releases sorbed P; nitrate-only N has the opposite effect
success_thresholds: No visible P-deficiency purpling at 30 days

phase_0_14_days: Mulch the entire slope with 5-8 t/ha straw/residue/compost before the next rainfall event
Staple jute/coir netting over all bare patches and active rill lines
Divert upslope runoff into a grassed off-take; cut a temporary grassed waterway (3-5 m) along the drainage line
Install check dams (brush/stone) in active rills to stop headcutting
phase_14_60_days: Survey contours with an A-frame/dumpy level; mark a line every 5-10 m vertical interval (5 m where slope > 15%)
Plant vetiver slips (Chrysopogon zizanioides) along every contour line - 2-3 slips per station, 0.3-0.5 m apart in-line; grass the waterway
On 5-10% slopes add contour bunds or tied ridges; on >15% slopes build bench terraces with grassed risers
Sow the cover crop / living mulch mix and the nurse crop the same day as the main planting
phase_60_90_days: Target >= 70% ground cover by Day 30 and 100% cover by Day 60
Hand-weed only; re-top-up mulch after any storm; inspect vetiver lines and clear any rill forming across them
Surface-apply 5-10 t/ha compost under mulch to rebuild the A horizon (never deep-incorporate on the slope)
standing_rules: No clean tillage, no burning, no downhill ploughing, no wheel traffic on wet soil
No bare inter-row soil after canopy closure
Harvest and replant the same week - never leave a harvested slope exposed

application_sequence.action: Soil test + buffer pH + slope survey; order lime, charged biochar, reactive rock phosphate, SSP, AMF, vetiver slips, mulch, planting stakes (guard G-02)
Apply 60-70% of the calcitic/dolomitic lime rate (type chosen from exchangeable Mg) under light incorporation or beneath mulch; begin co-composting biochar (1:2)
Emergency erosion works: mulch 5-8 t/ha, jute netting, check dams, vetiver contour lines, grassed waterways (guard G-04)

Make contour rows/beds; band reactive rock phosphate 250-400 kg/ha + SSP 200-300 kg/ha in the planting row; incorporate charged biochar 5-10 t/ha with 8-15 t/ha compost; band K 40-60 kg K2O/ha (pumice leaches K rapidly)
Spot re-test pH - confirm >= 5.5 before planting; if pH < 5.3 apply the remaining lime topdress and delay planting by 2 weeks
Prepare planting stakes/vines, set up protein trays, confirm contour structures and mulch are intact
Plant the main starch crop with AMF in the planting hole; plant the nurse/cover crop the same day; start the emergency protein relay
Verify: pH 5.5-6.0, Olsen P >= 12-15 mg/kg, ground cover >= 70% at Day 30 and 100% at Day 60; re-band P if deficient

emergency_protein_under_25_days.requirement: Edible protein available within 25 days of Day 0 (Day 0 = arrival/planting day)
emergency_protein_under_25_days.core_principle: Grow sprouts and microgreens OFF-SOIL in clean trays with plain water. This decouples emergency nutrition from the liming/reclamation programme: no soil, no pH dependence, no wait for lime to react, no erosion exposure. A soil-planted amaranth/legume-leaf relay is the backup layer.

system.production_unit: Shallow trays or a bench 0.5-1.0 m^2, shade house or covered area, clean water, no fertiliser needed
system.stagger_rule: Start new trays every 2-3 days from Day 0 (Day 0, 3, 6, 9...) so harvests overlap continuously to Day 25

space_per_person.unit: m^2 of tray area per person for the full 25-day window

system.environment: 20-25 C, indirect light; rinse with clean water 2-3 times per day; always drain fully - never let seed sit in standing water

crops.method: Soak seed 8-12 h; sow densely on a moist substrate or hydroponic mat; grow 10-15 cm; cut the top 8-10 cm leaving 2 nodes for a second cut 5-7 days later
crops.notes: Highest-yielding and most forgiving shoot crop; edible pods/seed are also food; untreated seed only

crops.method: Soak 6-8 h; sow in trays; cover 2-3 days in the dark to etiolate; rinse 2-3x/day; harvest when roots are 1-2 cm and the shoot is 5-10 cm
crops.notes: Fastest reliable protein in the system; dry seed is ~24% protein; keep dry-seed reserves as the long-term protein stock

crops.method: Soak 8-12 h; tray sprout with daily rinsing; harvest at 2-4 cm tail
crops.notes: Also cooks as a whole pulse at 12-14 days; tolerates cooler ambient temperatures

crops.method: Soak 6-8 h; tray sprout; rinse twice daily
crops.notes: Cowpea seed is acid-soil adapted and available locally; also sows into the field as the cover crop at Day 0

crops.method: Soak 12 h; sprout in a moist cloth or tray; rinse twice daily; harvest when tail equals seed length

starch_root_crop_strategy.selection_logic: The basin needs a long-term, high-yield, acid-tolerant survival staple that tolerates pH 4.6 and low-P andosol conditions, plus an immediate living-mulch crop that closes the slope cover gap within 45-60 days. The two are established together: cassava as the survival anchor, sweet potato as the nurse/erosion crop and first starch, taro for wet niches.

cultivation_roadmaps.total_duration_days: 300-365 (main harvest); protein secured within 25 days; first starch (sweet potato nurse) at 90-150 days
cultivation_roadmaps.planting_material: Vegetative stakes: 20-25 cm long, 5-8 nodes, pencil-thick, cut from healthy 6-12 month old lateral branches of disease-free mother plants; plant within 24-48 h of cutting; dip cut ends in wood ash or a labelled fungicide; rate 10,000-13,000 stakes/ha
cultivation_roadmaps.spacing: 1.0 m between rows x 0.8 m between plants (12,500 plants/ha); all rows on the contour

emergency_protein_plan.requirement: Edible protein by Day 25 from Day 0
emergency_protein_plan.method: Off-soil tray relay started the same day as planting (independent of the limed soil), plus an in-field leaf relay

Day 0: broadcast a 1-2 m^2 amaranth block in a moist, sheltered bed as the in-field backup
Day 3/6/9: sow staggered trays so harvests overlap
Day 8-12: harvest mung/lentil/cowpea sprouts - first protein met

phases.name: Diagnosis and Lime Requirement
steps: Take a composite soil sample (20-25 cores, 0-15 cm per management unit): pH, buffer pH (SMP/Kehres), ECe, exchangeable Al/Ca/Mg/K, Olsen or Truog P, organic C; request oxalate Al+Fe and P retention if available.
Record slope percent, ground cover percent and erosion class with the sample (photograph fixed reference points).
Compute the lime rate from BUFFER pH, not water pH (guard G-02). Default band for pH 4.6 is 2-4 t/ha CaCO3e; 4-6 t/ha if exchangeable Al > 2.5 cmol/kg.
Choose the lime type from exchangeable Mg: <1.0 cmol/kg = dolomitic (default for leached pumice basins); 1.0-1.5 = 50:50 blend; >1.5 = calcitic.
Confirm ECe < 0.75 dS/m (guard G-01) before committing to the programme.

Order inputs: lime, biochar feedstock for co-composting, reactive rock phosphate, SSP, charged biochar, K fertiliser, AMF inoculant, vetiver slips, mulch material, jute netting, cassava stakes, sweet potato vines, pea/mung/lentil seed.
phases.checkpoint: Buffer pH recorded; lime type decided; ECe confirmed non-saline

phases.name: Liming, Biochar Charging and Contour Works
steps: Broadcast 60-70% of the lime rate and work it into the top 0-15 cm by light rotavation or hand forking on beds; on slopes >5% spread it under the mulch layer or in contour furrows only - never plough on the fall line.
Start charging the biochar: co-compost biochar at 1:2 with manure/compost for 2-4 weeks, or soak in compost tea (never apply fresh biochar).
Emergency erosion works (guard G-04): mulch the whole slope 5-8 t/ha; staple jute/coir netting over bare ground and rills; cut brush check dams into active rills.
Mark contour lines every 5-10 m vertical interval (5 m on slopes >15%) with the A-frame; plant vetiver slips along each line (2-3 slips per station, 0.3-0.5 m apart in-line) and grass the waterway.
Surface-apply 5-10 t/ha compost under the mulch to start rebuilding the A horizon - do not deep-incorporate on the slope.
Wait: lime needs 4-8 weeks to react. Do not plant into unlimed soil when pH < 5.0.
phases.checkpoint: Slope fully covered before the next rain; vetiver lines planted; no bare soil visible

phases.name: Beds, Phosphorus Placement and Inoculation
steps: Spot re-test pH: proceed only at pH >= 5.5; if still < 5.3, apply the remaining lime topdress and delay planting by 2 weeks.
Make contour rows / broad beds 80-100 cm wide; on >15% slopes build bench terraces first.
Incorporate the charged biochar (5-10 t/ha) with 8-15 t/ha compost in the planting rows only.

Band phosphorus in the row: reactive rock phosphate 250-400 kg/ha at 10-15 cm depth plus SSP 200-300 kg/ha (40-60 kg P2O5) at 5 cm below and to the side of the future stake position - never broadcast (allophane would fix it).
Band K (40-60 kg K2O/ha) - pumice and ash leach potassium rapidly.
Prepare charged biochar as the AMF carrier: mix the granular inoculant 1:5 with charged biochar; keep it in the shade, dry and out of direct sun.
Prepare the emergency protein area: shade a bench or stack trays 0.4-0.5 m^2 per person, clean water and drainage.
Prepare nurse-crop material: sweet potato vine tips 25-35 cm with 3-4 nodes.
Confirm contour structures and mulch are intact before the first rain (guard G-04).
phases.checkpoint: pH >= 5.5 confirmed; P banded; beds and contours complete

phases.name: Planting and Day 0 Protein Relay
steps: Cut stakes on planting day from the stored bundle; reject any with rot, pith holes or pest damage.
Plant stakes on the contour at 1.0 x 0.8 m: insert about two-thirds of the stake (12-15 cm) with 1-2 nodes above ground, at a slight angle; firm the soil firmly around each stake.
Apply 20-50 g of AMF + charged biochar mix directly to the base of each stake as it is set.
Water each stake with 2-3 L to settle the soil.
SAME DAY: plant the sweet potato nurse crop in the alleys between cassava rows (80 cm rows x 30 cm, or broadcast vines on the flat) - this is the erosion cover and the first starch.
SAME DAY: sow emergency protein tray 1 (mung) and tray 2 (pea shoots), soak lentil/chickpea for the Day 3 stagger, broadcast the amaranth block - Day 0 of the 25-day protein clock.
Spread 5-8 t/ha mulch over all bare soil between rows.
Plant a cowpea cover row along each contour berm (20-30 kg/ha) for N fixation and additional cover.
Record planting date: every day count below is relative to Day 0.
inputs: Protein seed (mung, pea, lentil, chickpea) 3-5 kg total
checkpoints: No stake dislodged by wind/rain at Day 7

phases.name: Emergency Protein Window
steps: Trays: rinse 2-3x per day with clean water, drain fully, keep at 20-25 C in indirect light; discard any tray with slime, off smell or mould (food safety).
Harvest mung/lentil/cowpea sprouts at Day 8-12 when roots are 1-2 cm - first protein met; continue harvest from staggered trays every 2-3 days.
First pea shoot cut at Day 10-15 (cut the top 8-10 cm, leave 2 nodes); second cut Day 18-22.
Amaranth: thin to 2-3 cm at Day 7; first leaf cut at Day 20-25 (cut top 5 cm, leave 2 nodes); target 1.5-2.5 kg fresh leaf per m2 across the window.
Check cassava stakes for sprouting: replace any dead or rotted stakes with fresh ones at Day 10-14 (keep the hole count constant).
First weeding at Day 12-15 - by hand only, no tillage on the slope; re-mulch anything exposed.
Sweet potato: vines root and run; remove flower buds (flowering = stress); fill any gaps.
Water only if there has been no rain for 7-10 days; never waterlog (stake rot and root rot risk).
targets: Protein secured by Day 8-12 (sprouts) and closed by Day 25 (amaranth leaf)
Sweet potato ground cover > 40% by Day 25

phases.name: Establishment and Cover Closure
steps: Weed by hand or by smothering with mulch at Day 30-45 and Day 60-75 - never inter-row tillage (it re-opens the erosion window).
Top up mulch after every storm; keep total cover at or above 90%.
First nitrogen: only if the cassava leaves pale - 30 kg N/ha as a side dress at Day 45-60; the cowpea cover and residues normally supply enough for the first cycle.
Scout for cassava whitefly, mealybug, green mite and mosaic virus: destroy infested plants, use tolerant clones, and remove wild Ipomoea/weed hosts that carry pests.
Check vetiver lines and grassed waterways after each storm; clear any rill forming across a contour line within 48 hours.
Continue amaranth and cowpea leaf cuts every 7-10 days (protein layer).
Optional: lift a few baby sweet potatoes at Day 90-100 (target 100-200 g each) - first starch.
Sidedress banded P (20-30 kg P2O5/ha) at Day 45-60 for the allophane soil.
Target: full ground cover by Day 60 - from here the crop itself controls erosion.
targets: Ground cover >= 70% at Day 30, 100% at Day 60
Cassava canopy beginning to close at Day 90
No new rill extension since Day 0

phases.name: Canopy Closure and Tuber Bulking
steps: Stop all nitrogen after Day 90 (excess N produces leaves, not roots); all crop N should be applied within the first 60-90 days.
Sidedress potassium at Day 90-120 (60-80 kg K2O/ha) - K builds dry matter and is rapidly leached from pumice.
Harvest the main sweet potato nurse crop at Day 120-150 and IMMEDIATELY re-mulch the exposed alleys and sow a cowpea/Mucuna cover - a harvested slope must never be left bare.
Continue hand weeding; keep mulch at 5-8 t/ha; do not disturb the cassava root zone.
Inspect contour structures after every storm; repair vetiver gaps.
Monitor for cassava bacterial blight and anthracnose: remove and burn infected material, avoid wetting foliage late in the day.
Interplant taro suckers in wet drain margins and shaded terrace edges (Day 120-150) as the next starch layer.
Continue protein layer: dry-pulse harvest of mung/cowpea from Day 90.
targets: Sweet potato main crop lifted at Day 120-150 with immediate re-cover

phases.name: Harvest, Processing and Storage
steps: Test lift at Day 180-240 (baby harvest): target 1.5-2.5 kg per plant.
Main harvest at Day 270-360 when the lower leaves yellow and the skin of the oldest tuber is easy to score.

Harvest in small batches to the household's 2-3 day requirement - lifted roots deteriorate within 24-72 hours; the standing crop IS the storage (leave unlifted roots in the ground until needed, up to 12-18 months).
PROCESS BEFORE EATING (guard G-05): peel, cut into chips or shreds, soak in water 24-48 h (or ferment), rinse, then boil thoroughly or sun-dry; cook leaves 10-15 minutes. Never eat raw cassava.
Lift with a fork, avoiding punctures; keep stakes from selected healthy plants wrapped in damp material for the next cycle.
Record yield (target 15-25 t/ha first cycle on the reclaimed ash soil, 25-40 t/ha once the soil is fully remediated).
Store dried chips/flour in a cool, dry, rodent-proof container - keeps 6-12 months.
Post-harvest the same week: surface-spread 3-5 t/ha compost and sow a legume cover crop (Mucuna/Crotalaria) - never leave the slope bare.

phases.name: Post-Harvest and Year 2 Reset
steps: Re-test pH, buffer pH and Olsen P; re-lime with 0.5-1.5 t/ha CaCO3e if pH has drifted below 5.5.
Keep the cover crop growing through the off-season; plough it under only on terraces - on slopes cut and leave as mulch.
Rotate the following cycle: sweet potato or potato (after liming) in the rows where cassava was, with cassava on the alternate block.
Replenish vetiver hedgerows, repair bunds, and re-mulch before the next wet season.
Repeat the soil test annually; expect to top-dress lime every 1-2 years on leached pumice.
targets: Ground cover maintained at 100% year round

cultivation_roadmaps.annual_cycle_note: Emergency protein (off-soil sprouts + amaranth) occupies Day 0-25 and can start any time; the sweet potato nurse crop covers the slope and yields first starch at Day 90-150; cassava is the long-haul survival crop harvested from Day 270 with an in-ground reserve; cowpea/Mucuna cover closes the year so the slope is never bare.

volcanic_ash_pumice_basin.label: Degraded Volcanic Ash / High-Acid Pumice Basin - Emergency Scenario

diagnosis.base_condition: ACID_LOW_BASE (severity: high) - pH 4.6 falls in the STRONGLY_ACIDIC class (4.5-5.0), EC assumed non-saline
primary_limitations: Exchangeable Al3+ toxicity and low base saturation (Ca, Mg, K leached from ash and pumice)
Allophane / short-range-order mineral phosphate fixation - applied P is locked up
Severe slope erosion removing the ash topsoil that holds the little available P

treatment_sequence: 1. EROSION FIRST (Day -60): mulch 5-8 t/ha, jute netting over rills, vetiver contour hedgerows every 5-10 m vertical interval, grassed waterways, check dams.

2. LIME to pH 5.5-6.0 (target 5.8) at 2-4 t/ha CaCO3e (4-6 t/ha if Al > 2.5 cmol/kg), type chosen from exchangeable Mg: dolomitic if Mg < 1.0 cmol/kg (typical for leached pumice), 50:50 if 1.0-1.5, calcitic if > 1.5; apply 60-70% at Day -60, balance at Day +60; never with ammonium fertiliser.

3. BIOCHAR 5-10 t/ha, charged by co-composting 1:2 for 2-4 weeks (never fresh), incorporated in rows or surface-applied under mulch on slopes; deduct its 0.05-0.20 t/t liming credit from the lime rate.

4. PHOSPHORUS: reactive rock phosphate 250-400 kg/ha banded at 10-15 cm PLUS SSP 200-300 kg/ha (40-60 kg P2O5) banded in the planting zone; sidedress 20-30 kg P2O5/ha at Day 45-60; AMF inoculant 25-50 g per planting point carried on charged biochar; 8-15 t/ha compost as the sorption competitor.
5. PROTEIN (< 25 days): off-soil tray relay from Day 0 - pea shoots (Day 10-15), mung/lentil/cowpea sprouts (Day 8-12), amaranth leaf (Day 20-25), staggered every 2-3 days.
6. CROPS: cassava as the long-term survival starch (Day 0, contour rows, stakes 1.0 x 0.8 m), sweet potato as the nurse/erosion crop and first starch (Day 90-150), cowpea cover, taro in wet niches.
7. VERIFY: pH, Olsen P and ground cover at Day 14/45/60/90 per monitoring_plan.
